_about: Hand labels for eval/run_answer_replay.py (Decision 72). One labeller; see guide.

provenance.claims_from: python -m eval.run_answer_replay (main 3476281, --as-of pm-run, FactCG-DeBERTa-v3-Large fp16 on GPU, judge stubbed); runs pm and am, context-reproduced answers only
provenance.sample_rule: every flagged claim; random.Random(72).sample of 70 judge-bound and 70 locally passed claims (population sorted by key)

guide.reference: The nine documents of data/sample_deal (the whole data room), not the replayed context.
guide.unit: One claim exactly as src/verification/claims.py produced it (clean text), read in its answer: a bullet under a lead-in is read with the lead-in when the lead-in supplies its predicate ("The documents do not include: - Quarterly statements for FY2024" is the claim that the room lacks FY2024 quarterly statements).

labels.supported: Every assertion in the claim is stated in the documents, or follows from them by simple arithmetic (sum, difference, ratio, percentage change, multiple) correct to the precision written. Paraphrase is fine. A statement attributed to a document ("the QoE report notes ...") must be in that document. A figure on which documents disagree is supported when the claim states one document's value without contradicting itself or misattributing it. A statement of absence ("the documents do not disclose X") is supported when no document states X. A recommendation or inference is supported when it is a reasonable reading of what the documents say and the facts it relies on are right.
labels.not_supported: At least one assertion is contradicted by the documents, or is stated nowhere and does not follow from them: a wrong figure, period, party, document attribution or direction; a calculation that does not reproduce; a statement of absence about something a document does state; a fact the documents do not contain (even if plausible).
labels.not_checkable: Asserts nothing about the deal or the documents that could be true or false: a heading or label without a predicate ("Deductible / Basket Threshold", "Atlas Data Holdings (Private Equity Consortium - DECLINE)"), a formula fragment or a marker-only line ("(Derived/Computed metric) [COMPUTED: $716.6M / $92.8M]" is NOT this - it asserts a computation), generic advice not attributed to the documents ("Buyers should confirm X in diligence"), or a question restated.

guide.multi_fact: One wrong part makes the whole claim not_supported; the reason names the part.
guide.rounding: A figure rounded to the precision written is supported ($716.6M / $92.8M = 7.72x; 7.7x also fine). A figure stated more precisely than the documents allow is supported only if it reproduces.

causes._about: Recorded for every claim labelled supported or not_checkable that the verifier flags or leaves for the judge, and for every not_supported claim it passes. One primary cause.
causes.arithmetic: the claim states a correct derivation (written-out formula, a ratio or sum of document figures, a percentage change) that numeric grounding could not reproduce
causes.multi_fact: several facts in one claim, no single short premise window states them all
causes.table_without_headers: a table row (or Label: value line) whose cells only mean something with their column headers
causes.decline: a correct statement of absence phrased in a way the absence pattern misses, scored as an ordinary claim
causes.paraphrase: one fact, reworded beyond what the entailment model recognises
causes.conflict_in_documents: the documents disagree and the claim states one side
causes.inference: a reasonable inference or recommendation; no passage states it
causes.other: anything else; the note says what
causes.context_dependent: the claim's subject lives in a heading, a bullet lead-in or the previous sentence ('Procedural Posture: Mediation scheduled for May 2024' under the Hartley bullet; 'Amount: $13.92 million')
causes.date_from_header: the claim repeats the document's as-of date from its header, which no premise window holds
causes.absence_by_design: a statement of absence already recognised as one; it goes to the judge by design

guide.ambiguity: Labelled once by one labeller (no second annotator). Cases where the label turns on a judgement call carry ambiguous=true and a note; rates are also reported with those excluded.
guide.sampling: Strata are the BASELINE replay outcome (main at 3476281, as-of pm-run, FactCG): every flagged claim and every judge-bound claim of reproduced answers is labelled (or a seeded sample of the judge stratum where noted), plus a seeded random sample (random.Random(72)) of locally passed claims. Each label carries its stratum; rates weight a label by stratum population / labelled count.
